expectations.text: Applies top-down scoping: significant accounts/disclosures → business processes → applications that initiate/record/process/report, consistent with AS 2201's risk-based approach
expectations.evidence: "Scoping is top-down and risk-based (AS 2201 ¶21-34 logic)... start from the financial statements and work down"; Steps 1→2→3 accounts→processes→applications performing "initiation/authorization/recording/processing/reporting"

expectations.text: Scopes the named systems sensibly: NetSuite (GL) and the billing engine (revenue) clearly in; Workday in for payroll-to-GL; the data warehouse in because finance relies on its revenue reports (IPE)
expectations.evidence: Table scopes NetSuite ("Books of record"), billing engine ("Directly initiates/records revenue"), Workday ("payroll, a significant expense account"), warehouse ("an IPE... source, in scope even though it doesn't 'process' the transaction")

expectations.text: Extends to supporting layers: database, OS/platform, and the access/change/operations ITGC processes for each in-scope application
expectations.evidence: "scope the database, OS/platform (including cloud IaaS/PaaS), and the ITGC processes at each layer"; billing engine "access, change management, and operations controls"

expectations.text: Handles outsourced layers via SOC 1 Type II reports: period coverage vs fiscal year, bridge letters for gaps, and mapping CUECs into the company's own control set
expectations.evidence: "get the SOC 1 Type II report, confirm the period covers your fiscal year (bridge letter needed for gaps)... map every complementary user-entity control (CUEC) into your own control set — an unmapped CUEC is a control gap"

expectations.text: Covers IPE/EUC: reports used in controls need accuracy/completeness validation, and control-relevant spreadsheets enter scope
expectations.evidence: IPE validation covered ("validate the source data, the transformation logic... and the parameters") but no mention of EUC/control-relevant spreadsheets entering scope
